name: Primary Melanoma of the Central Nervous System

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary CNS Melanoma

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of melanoma cells within CNS tissue
No evidence of primary melanoma outside the central nervous system after thorough dermatological and systemic evaluation
MRI or CT imaging showing solitary or multiple CNS lesions with melanotic features
Positive immunohistochemical staining for melanoma markers such as HMB-45, S-100, and Melan-A

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of melanoma within CNS tissue plus absence of extracranial primary melanoma and supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of metastatic melanoma is critical to diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits correlating with lesion location

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment or altered mental status

searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
back pain with nerve compression signs
weakness or numbness from spinal cord squeezing

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: CSF analysis may show elevated protein and presence of malignant melanocytic cells
Immunohistochemical positivity for HMB-45, S-100, Melan-A
imaging: MRI showing hyperintense lesions on T1-weighted images due to melanin content
Contrast-enhancing CNS masses on MRI or CT
genetic: Mutations in BRAF, NRAS, or KIT genes may be present but less characterized in primary CNS melanoma
other: Exclusion of extracranial primary melanoma by dermatological and systemic imaging evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of known primary cutaneous or mucosal melanoma
Multiple CNS lesions with systemic metastases
Histopathology showing meningioma cells with melanin pigment
Different immunohistochemical profile (EMA positive, melanoma markers negative)

redFlags: New onset seizures in adult without prior history
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Kumar N, et al. Primary CNS melanoma: a review of clinical features and management. J Neurooncol. 2020;147(3):467-475.
Orphanet Report on Primary Melanoma of the Central Nervous System, ORPHA:252050.
